title: A definition excerpt must retain its binding decorators
applies_when: Python source is shortened for a model or a targeted reproduction using AST function line ranges, particularly properties, class/static methods and decorated native/JIT wrappers.
lesson: Audit the supplied evidence before implementing its predicted bug. FunctionDef.lineno can start at def, omitting earlier decorators. A body containing def should_run without @property looks like a truthy bound method; the actual Schedule Job exposes a boolean property, so run_pending is correct without parentheses. Prefer the existing requested definition selector over a task-local AST slicer, retain decorators and original line ranges, and inspect the actual package. Keep malformed packets and their model costs as preparation failures rather than counting a proposed repair as a discovery. Structured JSON acceptance does not verify a model's runtime claim or its restatement of test accounting; collected total minus skips is not the total number of passing tests.
avoid_when: An ordinary fixed source window can legitimately be partial; mark that limitation instead of inferring an omitted decorator is absent. Retaining syntax does not resolve inherited/dynamic binding, imports, defaults, wrappers or caller reachability. The regular Scout requested-definition selector already preserves decorators; a task-local clipping failure does not prove that reader is broken. This mechanism and counterexample do not establish a measured reduction in false positives, improved PR conversion or prospective model-comparison results.

evidence.note: AST documentation represents function decorators separately in decorator_list. Review the source span and decorator syntax rather than treating a function body alone as its complete binding contract.
Pinned run_pending reads job.should_run, and Job.should_run is decorated with @property. This source contradicts the bound-method premise; it is not a new Schedule bug or performance result.
